description: A post: one thing a person publishes, with a Markdown body, optional attachments, and optional information about where it first appeared. These fields are fixed and the same on every site; a site adds its own under `site`.

subtitle.description: An optional line shown under the title.

body.description: CommonMark, with footnotes ([^1] in the text and [^1]: for the note). Use media:ID as an image destination to place an attachment at that point in the body. The ID refers to an entry in this post's media array.

updatedAt.description: When the post was last changed after it was published.

canonicalUrl.description: The post's address on the author's public website. It is the same whoever can see the post: a post that is not public holds the address it would have if it were.

slug.description: The last part of the post's address on the author's website: lowercase Latin letters and digits joined by single hyphens. It can be changed, and the record stays the same record. A record with no slug uses its own key.

form.description: What kind of object this post is, identified from its format. A writing has a title and free-form content; a note has no title. An image, gallery, video, audio, file, or media post holds only attachments. A link, embed, quote, list, or code post holds only that. Other is anything else. The list can grow: treat a form you do not know as other, and show the title, body, and attachments.

label.description: The author's name for the section of their site this post belongs to, such as Writings or Photographs. Free-form.

sublabel.description: The author's name for a group inside the label, such as a series or an album. Free-form.

connect.description: What this post branches from: earlier posts or web pages. Each entry is an AT URI or an HTTP(S) URL.

link.description: For a link or embed post: the page it points to, as that page described itself when the post was made.

source.description: Where this post first appeared, if not on the author's own website.

site.description: Optional data the fixed fields have no place for. An object whose $type names the schema that declares each of its fields. This is the only place for anything the fixed schema does not define.

media.description: Attachments keyed by IDs unique within this post. References in the body determine their placement. The kinds can grow: skip an attachment of a kind you do not know.

siteName.description: The name of the website the page is on.

image.description: A copy of the page's preview image.

platform.description: The identifier of the platform the post first appeared on, in lower case, such as substack.

uri.description: The post's address on that platform.

id.description: The platform's own identifier for the post.

file.description: A copy of the image kept in the author's repository. It may be smaller than the original.

sourceUrl.description: Where the original lives or came from, when that is somewhere other than this repository.

file.description: A copy of the video kept in the author's repository. It may be smaller than the original.

sourceUrl.description: Where the original lives or came from, when that is somewhere other than this repository.

poster.description: A still image shown before the video plays.

file.description: A copy of the recording kept in the author's repository.

sourceUrl.description: Where the original lives or came from, when that is somewhere other than this repository.

file.description: A copy of the file kept in the author's repository.

sourceUrl.description: Where the original lives or came from, when that is somewhere other than this repository.
